claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 17, his eligibility depends on his current situation. Could you please tell me if Alex is currently in one of the following:

1. Full-time non-advanced education (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs up to level 3, or similar)
2. An approved training programme (such as a traineeship in England, or a government-funded training programme in Wales or Scotland)
3. Neither of the above (e.g., working full-time, in higher education like university, or not in education/training)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex isn't in education anymore - he left school and he's working full-time now at a local warehouse.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about Alex's situation.

I have one more question to confirm: When did Alex leave school and start working full-time? Specifically, was it:

1. Before the end of August following his 16th birthday, or
2. After the end of August following his 16th birthday?

This helps determine the exact end date for any Child Benefit entitlement.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school last summer, just after his GCSEs finished. So that would have been before the end of August after he turned 16, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Based on the information you've provided, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

**Alex (age 17):** Child Benefit can continue for children aged 16-19, but only if they remain in:
- Full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels, T-levels, or NVQs up to level 3), or
- An approved training programme

Since Alex left school after his GCSEs and is now working full-time at a warehouse, he no longer meets the criteria for Child Benefit. The benefit would have stopped at the end of August following his 16th birthday when he left education.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he returns to full-time non-advanced education or starts an approved training programme—you may be able to claim again at that point.

Is there anything else you'd like to know?

reasonings: Alex is 17 years old and left school before the end of August following his 16th birthday to work full-time. Child Benefit normally continues until the 31st of August following a child's 16th birthday if they leave education. Since Alex left school and started full-time work before this date, and is not in approved education or training, he no longer qualifies as a child for Child Benefit purposes. Child Benefit can only continue for 16-19 year olds if they remain in full-time non-advanced education or approved training. As Alex is working full-time and not in qualifying education or training, he is not eligible for Child Benefit.
